Introduction

This is a project that analyzes worldwide terrorism rates. It uses the ‘Global Terrorism Database’ which contains cases of terrorism from 1970 - 2017 (excluding 1993). It has over 100 variables on information such as locations, outcomes, etc. The sources for the data in the data set are from unclassified media articles, so it is influenced by access to these media articles. The database is funded by START, the US Department of State and the US Department of Homeland Security Science and Technology Directorate’s Office of University Programs.

Code chunks can have code other than R. We can use css here to center our title.

h1 {
  text-align: center;

The first thing we’ll do is import the libraries we’ll use to analyze the data in the dataset.

knitr::opts_chunk$set(warning = FALSE, message = FALSE)

library(ggplot2)

#gganimate builds on ggplot, allowing us to animate our graphs 
library(gganimate)

#leaflet is a library for building interactive maps 
library(leaflet)

#a library that allows us to work with GIS data in r 
library(rgdal)

#a library that allows us to do things with colours 
library(RColorBrewer)

Then we’ll import the data into R from our computer.

Basic Analysis

The data set is very large and has many variables, so for some basic analysis, let’s find the countries with the most occurrences of terrorism from 1970-2017. We can see Iraq has had the most cases of terrorism.

#Counts the total occurrences of countries in the dataframe  
Instances <- data %>% count(country_txt)

#Arranges the countries in descending order and gets the top 10
top10Instances <- Instances %>% arrange(desc( n))
top10Instances <- top10Instances[1:10,]

#Plots the data as a bar graph 
ggplot(top10Instances, aes(x = country_txt, y = n)) + geom_col() + labs(x = 'Country', y = 'Instances', title = 'Top 10 Countries With Most Instances of Terrorism (1970-2017)')

The same can also be done to find the countries with the least amount of terrorism occurrences. Note: all countries have had at least 1 terrorism case, and it was more than a 5 way tie to show up in the graph.

#Finds the top 5 countries with the least instances 
least5Instances <- Instances %>% arrange(n)
least5Instances <- least5Instances[1:5,]

#Plots the data as a bar graph 
ggplot(least5Instances, aes(x = country_txt, y = n)) + geom_col() + labs(x = 'Country', title = 'Top 5 Countries With Least Instances of Terrorism (1970-2017)') + scale_y_continuous(name = 'Instances', limits = c(0,3))

Animating Trends Over Time

We can also see the number of attacks per year. After around the year 2005, attacks significantly increased.

#Makes a dataframe that has the year and terrorism instance count for that year 
yearCount <- count(data, iyear)

#changes the column names
colnames(yearCount)[2] <- 'totalAttacks'
colnames(yearCount)[1] <- 'year'
  
#saves an animation
#Pipes a ggplot line graph into a function to animate it. 
animation <- ggplot(yearCount, aes(x = year, y = totalAttacks)) + geom_line( color = "#FF6666") + geom_point() + transition_reveal(year)

#Animates the line graph of 100 frames at 7 frames per second 
animate(animation, nframes = 100, fps = 7)

Finding Success to Failure Ratio and Most Successful Groups

We can filter for only terrorist groups that have had successful attacks.

#Filters for only the attacks that were successful 
groupSuccessful <- data %>% filter(success == 1) %>% select(gname, success)

#Counts the successes of groups
numberOfSuccesses <- groupSuccessful %>% count(gname) %>% arrange(desc(n))

#changes column names 
colnames(numberOfSuccesses)[2] <- "Successes" 
colnames(numberOfSuccesses)[1] <- "Group Names"

We can also find the groups that have had the most attacks.

#Counts the group that appears the most in dataset
numberOfAttacks <- data %>% count(gname) %>% arrange(desc(n))

#changes column names 
colnames(numberOfAttacks)[2] <- 'Attacks'
colnames(numberOfAttacks)[1] <- 'Group Names' 

#turns the dataframe into a paged table  
numberOfAttacks %>% rmarkdown::paged_table()

Now we can find what terrorist groups have the best success to failure ratios.

#lines up the 'numberOfAttacks' column and 'numberOfSuccesses' column by group names
successRate <- merge(numberOfAttacks, numberOfSuccesses, by.x = 'Group Names')

#creates a new column in dataframe that represents the success rates 
successRate <- mutate(successRate, Ratio = successRate[[3]]/successRate[[2]])

#arranges in descending order of success ratio 
successRate <- successRate %>% arrange(desc(Ratio),desc(Attacks))

#turns the dataframe into a paged table  
successRate %>% rmarkdown::paged_table()

Let’s say we’re interested in seeing the success rates of terrorist groups that are active and large enough to have more than 50 attacks.

#selects only the groups with more than 50 attempted attacks 
bigSuccessRate <- successRate %>% filter(Attacks > 50)

#arranges in descending order 
bigSuccessRate <- bigSuccessRate %>% arrange(desc(Ratio))

#turns the dataframe into a paged table  
bigSuccessRate %>% rmarkdown::paged_table()

We can slightly change the code to view the information in ascending order instead now.

#arranges in ascending order 
smallSuccessRate <- bigSuccessRate %>% arrange(Ratio)

#turns the dataframe into a paged table  
smallSuccessRate %>% rmarkdown::paged_table()

It appears the Maoists have carried out quite a few terrorist attacks, I wonder where they geographically happened. We can first make a data frame that only include attacks carried out by maoists.

#makes a dataframe that only contains attacks carried out by maoists 
maoists <- data %>% filter(gname == 'Maoists')

Making an Interactive Map

Now we can plot all of them on an interactive map.

#downloads the map template, we only need to download it once 
#download.file("http://thematicmapping.org/downloads/TM_WORLD_BORDERS_SIMPL-0.3.zip" , destfile="world_shape_file.zip")
#system("unzip world_shape_file.zip")

#loading spatial data 
world_spdf <- readOGR( 
  #finds where the shapefile is located 
  dsn = getwd(), 
  #layer is the name of shapefile 
  layer = "TM_WORLD_BORDERS_SIMPL-0.3",
  #don't want to print a message
  verbose = FALSE
)

#makes a new column in maoists dataframe that represents the number of people wounded 
maoists <- maoists %>% mutate(ncasualties = (nkill + nwound))
  
#define colorpalette for markers and chart legend
#values for which colour will change 
paletteBins <- c(1, 5, 10, 20, 30, 50, 100)

#palette is 'yellow to red'
#domain = NULL means 
colorPalette <- colorBin(palette = "YlOrRd", domain = NULL,  bins = paletteBins, na.color = 'transparent')

#converts the columns to a numeric value for plotting   
maoists$latitude <- as.numeric(maoists$latitude)
maoists$longitude <- as.numeric(maoists$longitude)

#leaflet function takes in the template and adds things onto it 
leaflet(world_spdf) %>% 
  addTiles() %>% 
  setView(lat = 0, lng = 0, zoom = 2) %>% 
  #adds circles onto template
  #takes in the dataframe vectors and creates circle on map for each row in dataframe
  addCircles(       lng = ~maoists$longitude,
                    lat = ~maoists$latitude ,
                    radius = ~(((maoists$ncasualties)+10)**2.5),
                    weight = 1,
                    opacity = 1, 
                    color = ~colorPalette(maoists$ncasualties),
                    fillColor = ~colorPalette(maoists$ncasualties),
                    
                    fillOpacity = 0.8, 
                    
                    label = ~lapply(maoists$summary, htmltools::HTML)) %>% 
    #makes the legend 
    addLegend(pal = colorPalette, values = maoists$ncasualties, opacity=0.9, title = "Attacks", position = "bottomleft")
